approachQuestion.prompt:
Interleave the Ends of a Manifest

A finite acyclic singly linked list has original nodes L0,L1,...,L(n-1). Return the same nodes ordered L0,L(n-1),L1,L(n-2),... until every node appears once. Preserve each value, change only next links, and end the result in null. Input is head, not n; 0 <= n <= 200000.

Input: A -> B -> C -> D -> E. Output: A -> E -> B -> D -> C -> null.
Input: A -> B -> C -> D. Output: A -> D -> B -> C -> null. Empty input returns null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Reverse the full input and return it.
options.feedback: For A -> B -> C, the required head is A and order A,C,B, not C,B,A.

options.text: Split into the same two halves but weave them without reversing the second half.
options.feedback: For A -> B -> C -> D -> E this starts A,D rather than A,E, so it does not select the original last node first.

options.text: Use two runners to split into a first half of ceiling(n/2) nodes and a second half of floor(n/2) nodes, cutting their link. Iteratively reverse the second half, then weave its nodes one at a time between first-half nodes, saving both next references before each insertion.
options.feedback: The reversed second half supplies the outermost remaining end each time; the larger first half retains the unpaired middle node.

options.text: Copy all node references into an array, take alternating leftmost and rightmost references into the required order, and relink them with a null final next.
options.feedback: This builds the correct order but uses avoidable storage when half-reversal and weaving are permitted.

feedback.reason: The reversed second half supplies the outermost remaining end each time; the larger first half retains the unpaired middle node.

Cut the two halves before weaving so old links cannot create cycles. Reverse the second half, then save both successors before inserting each outer-end node. An odd-length first half keeps its final middle node.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-22-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Midpoint search, half reversal and weaving each perform at most linear work. Weaving a long list requires linear link changes. The halves are cut before merging, all reversals are iterative, and only fixed references are retained; the output uses original nodes.
